v.rationale: All three take essentially the same approach and all pass their suites. They share one real bug: the rate-limit key is built from the raw email input before validation, so an array email returns 500 instead of 422 (confirmed by probe). Other probes (form-encoded clients, padded emails, a sixth successful login, 429 responses) behaved the same across all three. With no distinguishing bugs, the ranking comes down to idiom and tests. impl-3 has the most thorough Pest tests (describe blocks, a reset-window test with travel, a check that the other token survives a revoke) and uses validated(). impl-1 also uses validated() and has the tidiest limiter key, but its per-IP test is weak. impl-2 is the simplest but passes Stringable request values straight into query and token creation instead of validated data, and sets up RefreshDatabase per file.
